title: Google Business Profile for Real Estate Agents and Channel Partners
seoTitle: Google Business Profile for Real Estate Agents & CPs
excerpt: How brokers and channel partners can set up and grow a Google Business Profile: categories, service areas, photos, posts and asking for reviews the right way.

inlineImages.alt: A woman smiling while talking on her phone

faqs.question: Why does a Google Business Profile matter for real estate agents?
faqs.answer: Local searches like “property dealer near me” show map results first. A well-kept profile is one of the cheapest sources of local enquiries.

faqs.question: How does Google rank local results?
faqs.answer: Mainly on relevance, distance and prominence — how well the profile matches the search, how close you are, and how well known and reviewed you are.

faqs.question: Can I add keywords to my business name?
faqs.answer: No. Use your real business name exactly as on your signboard and documents. Keyword stuffing breaks Google’s guidelines and can get the profile suspended.

faqs.question: Which category should a real estate agent choose?
faqs.answer: “Real estate agency” or “Real estate agent” as the primary category, and “Real estate consultant” as an additional one if it fits.

faqs.question: Should I show my office address?
faqs.answer: Show it if clients visit your office. If you meet clients at sites, set up as a service-area business, hide the address and list the areas you cover.

faqs.question: How should I ask clients for reviews?
faqs.answer: Ask every client for an honest review with a direct link sent on WhatsApp. Don’t offer incentives, write reviews yourself, or ask only happy clients — Google prohibits fake and selectively solicited reviews.

faqs.question: What should the profile link to?
faqs.answer: A page explaining what you do and the projects you handle, with WhatsApp and call buttons — and for project posts, the project’s landing page.
